name: Knee Arthroscopy with Partial Meniscectomy — Molina NJ NJ-KA-29881

branches.initial: Initial request for knee arthroscopy with partial meniscectomy

criteria.description: Medical necessity for CPT 29881 knee arthroscopy with partial meniscectomy. ALL of diagnosis, functional limitation, imaging-or-exam, and failed conservative therapy must be met.

policy_citation.quote: Authorization is approved when ALL of the following criteria are met

children.description: Diagnosis of derangement of meniscus (ICD-10 M23.2*) confirmed by clinical evaluation.

policy_citation.quote: Diagnosis of derangement of meniscus (ICD-10 M23.2*) confirmed by clinical evaluation

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for a Condition with ICD-10 code matching M23.2* (e.g., M23.200 generic, M23.20X laterality-specific subcodes).

verdict_rubric.met: Patient has a documented Condition resource with ICD-10 code matching M23.2*.
verdict_rubric.not_met: Patient's diagnoses do not include any M23.2* code.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Diagnosis narrative suggests meniscal pathology but no ICD-10 code is attached.
verdict_rubric.not_documented: No diagnostic information available in records.

children.description: Documented functional limitation from the meniscal condition (inability to perform ADLs, knee instability, or pain interfering with daily activity).

policy_citation.quote: Functional limitation documented, including but not limited to inability to perform activities of daily living due to knee instability or pain

evaluation.extraction_hints: Find clinician narrative describing impairment of ADLs, work limitation, knee buckling/locking, or pain-limited activity. Functional-status assessments (KOOS, Lysholm) also qualify if available.

verdict_rubric.met: Specific ADL or activity limitation is documented (e.g., stair-climbing difficulty, knee giving way, work restriction).
verdict_rubric.not_met: Patient explicitly reports preserved function and no activity limitation.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Generic 'knee pain' documented without specific functional impact.
verdict_rubric.not_documented: No assessment of functional status in records.

children.description: Either MRI evidence of meniscal pathology OR positive provocative exam findings.

policy_citation.quote: At least one of the following must be present

children.description: MRI demonstrating a meniscal tear or other meniscal pathology.

policy_citation.quote: MRI demonstrating meniscal tear or meniscal pathology

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for a knee MRI report describing meniscal tear, degeneration, root tear, bucket-handle tear, or other meniscal pathology.

verdict_rubric.met: Knee MRI report explicitly describes meniscal tear or meniscal pathology.
verdict_rubric.not_met: MRI of the knee shows no meniscal pathology.
verdict_rubric.unclear: MRI describes intrasubstance signal abnormality without clear tear; report wording ambiguous.
verdict_rubric.not_documented: No MRI of the knee available.

children.description: Positive provocative physical-exam findings consistent with meniscal tear (e.g., McMurray, Thessaly, joint-line tenderness).

policy_citation.quote: Clinical examination findings consistent with meniscal tear, including positive provocative tests such as McMurray test or Thessaly test

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for documented positive McMurray test, Thessaly test, Apley grind, or joint-line tenderness recorded on physical exam.

verdict_rubric.met: Physical exam documents a positive McMurray, Thessaly, or equivalent provocative finding.
verdict_rubric.not_met: Physical exam documented but provocative tests are negative.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Exam mentions 'tenderness' or 'pain with motion' without naming a specific test.

children.description: Failed conservative therapy: documented NSAID trial AND documented PT (or contraindication).

policy_citation.quote: All of the following must be documented

children.description: Trial of NSAID therapy for a minimum of 4 weeks.

policy_citation.quote: Trial of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) therapy for a minimum of 4 weeks

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, meloxicam, celecoxib, ketorolac, etc. Validate the trial is at least 4 weeks via start/end dates or duration narrative.

verdict_rubric.met: NSAID from the standard class documented for at least 4 weeks (dates or explicit duration).
verdict_rubric.not_met: NSAID documented but duration is <4 weeks.
verdict_rubric.unclear: NSAID documented but duration ambiguous; or non-NSAID analgesic only.

children.description: Completed PT (≥6 sessions on the affected knee) OR documented contraindication to PT.
Completion of at least 6 physical therapy sessions targeting the affected knee.

policy_citation.quote: completion of a minimum of 6 physical therapy sessions directed at the affected knee

evaluation.extraction_hints: Find PT note documenting session count for the affected knee. Acceptable evidence: PT discharge summary, count of visits, or progress note referencing completed sessions.

verdict_rubric.met: PT records or narrative show ≥6 completed sessions targeting the affected knee.
verdict_rubric.not_met: PT documented but fewer than 6 sessions completed.
verdict_rubric.unclear: PT mentioned without session count, or sessions targeted a different body region.

children.description: Documented clinical contraindication to physical therapy.

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for explicit clinician statement that PT is contraindicated (e.g., recent fracture, severe instability, comorbidity making weight-bearing PT unsafe).

verdict_rubric.met: Clinician explicitly documents a contraindication to PT for this patient.
verdict_rubric.not_met: No contraindication; PT is expected per usual care.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Patient declined PT citing inconvenience or cost without a clinical contraindication.

exclusions.description: Acute traumatic tear requiring emergent surgical intervention (injury within 72 hours requiring immediate stabilization) — emergency pathway, not PA.

policy_citation.quote: The condition is an acute traumatic tear requiring emergent surgical intervention (defined as injury within 72 hours requiring immediate surgical stabilization)

evaluation.extraction_hints: Look for date of injury within 72 hours of submission AND clinician note indicating emergent surgical need (gross instability, locked knee with mechanical block).

verdict_rubric.met: Injury within 72 hours and clinician documents emergent surgical need.
verdict_rubric.not_met: Chronic or subacute meniscal injury; not emergent.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Recent injury (<72h) but no documentation of emergent need.
verdict_rubric.not_documented: Injury timing or emergent status not addressed.

exclusions.description: Primary indication is non-meniscal pathology (isolated chondral defect, ligamentous injury without meniscal involvement).

policy_citation.quote: The primary indication is non-meniscal pathology (e.g., isolated chondral defect, ligamentous injury without meniscal involvement)

evaluation.extraction_hints: Check imaging and clinical assessment for isolated chondral defect, ACL/PCL/MCL/LCL injury, or other non-meniscal pathology being the primary surgical indication.

verdict_rubric.met: Primary indication documented is non-meniscal (chondral, ligamentous) and meniscus is incidental.
verdict_rubric.not_met: Meniscal pathology is clearly the primary indication.
verdict_rubric.unclear: Both meniscal and non-meniscal findings present; primary indication not stated.
verdict_rubric.not_documented: Indication not clearly differentiated in records.

metadata.notes: Models Molina NJ Clinical Policy NJ-KA-29881 (Knee Arthroscopy with Partial Meniscectomy).
